doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Teaching at NOCCA and learning to teach from his own life
summary: After years as a band director, the last twenty at the arts school made it click once he taught from lived experience.

venues.name: New Orleans Center for Creative Arts

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That’s terrific. I know your name shows up a lot if you’re looking about other musicians and “was a student of” and it has your name a lot.

Yeah. Yeah I was blessed with having been in that particular situation teaching at the arts school in New Orleans. Half of my career has been in like a regular band director capacity which I used to hate because we had to do football games and parades and all this stuff man. I did it but it wasn’t my cup of — you know I had good concert bands but © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

once I started teaching at the art school for the last twenty years or so is like when it all came together for me. But I use all that experience to bring to the situation I was in, whatever I’m in. You know, when I got to the school, the New Orleans Center for the Creative Arts, at first I didn’t know what to do as I was trying to teach a certain way and it took me maybe a year or two years to really realize that I have to teach from my own experiences. So once I started doing that it took off man. I have to teach from my life. Because there are a lot of musicians and teachers rather, who are trying to teach certain things and didn’t even live the life so they don’t even know what it is. You know you’ve got to be out there, you have to have those experiences because you have to have something to draw from. And there are some of them who are teaching from what they read in a book.
